raw_response:
*Let me think about this season on my 60 mu...*

I'm 48, been in these fields since I was a boy following my old man around. Forty years. My wife works with me; both our sons are down south in the factories, only come back for Spring Festival. So it's mostly the two of us, and I hire neighbors when things get heavy — cotton picking, peanut digging.

My 60 mu is in three pieces. The western plot, about 15 mu, has been cotton since before I got married — that sandy soil works for it. The biggest piece, 25 mu toward the river, I put in peanuts. Peanuts do well on that land, and after the county started pushing us toward peanut and oil crops a few years back, the price has been decent enough. The last 20 mu, closer to the house, I keep in wheat then maize after — same as everybody around here.

**Wheat (the 20 mu by the house)** — I put it in last October like always. Jimai variety, whatever the shop had. About 12 kg seed per mu. I put down 2 bags of compound fertilizer (50 kg, 15-15-15 stuff) per mu before drilling with the seeder — that's how my father did it and that's what works. Wheat is through winter now, looking alright. When it starts jointing in mid-March, I'll spread about 20 kg urea on top. If it looks yellow in patches I'll put more there. I water with the well — once before winter, once at green-up, once at jointing, and one more at heading if no rain comes. Last April was dry and the pumping bill hurt. Hoping for 400 kg/mu again, same as last year.

**Maize (same 20 mu, after wheat)** — Soon as the combine finishes wheat around June 10, I rotavate and plant the same day if I can. No time to plow. Hybrid seed from the shop, whatever Zhengdan they have. I drop compound with the seed and topdress urea when it's at big flaring. Summer maize usually gets by on the rainy season, but I'll give it one irrigation if July goes dry. Hoping for around 450 kg/mu.

**Cotton (western 15 mu)** — Planting mid-April once the cold snap passes. I use improved seed, about 2 kg/mu. Compound at base, urea topdressed at squaring. Cotton's trouble is bugs. Bollworm, aphids, thrips — I spray whatever Old Chen at the agri shop says works this year. Probably 5-6 sprays through the season. Picking is backbreaking; me and the wife start in September, and I pay three or four neighbors by the kilo for the big picks. Hoping 250 kg/mu of lint.

**Peanut (25 mu, the big piece)** — This is my main crop. Plant late April after the cotton goes in. Seed runs me about 120 yuan/mu — I don't save my own peanut seed anymore, the county seed is better. Peanuts don't want much nitrogen — they make their own, old people always said — but they want phosphate and calcium. I put down compound plus calcium superphosphate at planting. Water once or twice if it's dry in June-July. Spray for leaf spot and aphids maybe twice. Hoping for 300 kg/mu of pods. If the price holds around 5 yuan/jin like last autumn, this is what pays for the kids' living allowance and keeps some cash back for winter.

My total cash out will be around 26-27 thousand yuan this year. That's tight but we've got it. If cotton prices come up this year or peanut holds, we'll be okay. If the well runs low in July like two years ago, everything changes.
